title: EU Approves Sanctions on Violent Israeli Settlers and Hamas Leaders — First Package in 21 Months
detail: All 27 EU foreign ministers approved new sanctions on May 11, 2026 targeting violent Israeli settlers and organizations supporting them in the West Bank, alongside sanctions against Hamas leaders. Seven settlers and settler organizations were blacklisted with asset freezes and travel bans; Hamas representatives were also targeted. The approval came after Hungary's new government under Prime Minister Péter Magyar lifted the veto that outgoing PM Viktor Orbán had imposed, enabling unanimous consensus for the first time. It was the first EU settler sanctions package in 21 months, with the previous round dating to July 2024. Proposals to sanction Israeli ministers Itamar Ben-Gvir and Bezalel Smotrich were dropped due to opposition from several member states. EU High Representative Kaja Kallas had signaled ahead of the vote that the bloc expected to approve the measures. The sanctions come as West Bank settler violence has reached record levels, with 59 communities fully depopulated, over 1,150 Palestinians killed, and the UN OHCHR characterizing the situation as a potential 'mass forcible transfer.'

media.caption: EU foreign ministers unanimously approve sanctions on violent Israeli settlers and Hamas leaders, May 11, 2026

title: IDF Releases Drone Strike Footage: Kfir Brigade UAV Kills IED-Planting Operative in Southern Gaza
detail: The Israel Defense Forces on May 11, 2026 released footage of a drone strike carried out in the Khan Yunis area of southern Gaza targeting a Palestinian operative who was planting an improvised explosive device. The operation was authorized by an IDF Kfir Brigade officer after a UAV operator reported an urgent incident in 'sector 900' that posed a potential threat to ground troops. The strike was coordinated between the Israeli Air Force and the Kfir Brigade operating on the ground inside the ceasefire zone. The footage showed the operative being engaged and the strike resulting in a confirmed direct hit. The incident is part of a continuing pattern of IDF operations under the October 2025 ceasefire, under which Israel characterizes targeted strikes against individuals it deems 'imminent threats' as permitted under self-defense provisions of the ceasefire framework. Hamas has characterized such operations as systematic violations of the ceasefire agreement.

media.caption: IDF releases drone footage of Kfir Brigade UAV strike on IED operative in Khan Yunis, southern Gaza, May 11, 2026

title: Spanish-Palestinian Flotilla Activist Saif Abukeshek Returns to Barcelona After Six Days in Israeli Custody
detail: Spanish-Palestinian activist Saif Abukeshek arrived back in Barcelona on May 11, 2026, defiant after six days in Israeli custody following his arrest during the Israeli navy's interception of the Global Sumud Flotilla in international waters near Crete. Abukeshek had been detained when Israeli naval forces boarded and seized the flotilla approximately 600 nautical miles from Gaza in late April 2026. He was transferred to Ashkelon, where he and Brazilian activist Thiago Ávila appeared before an Israeli court on May 3 alleging mistreatment and initiating a hunger strike; their detentions were extended 72 hours at that hearing. Upon release, Abukeshek returned to Spain with defiance, telling reporters he was committed to continuing to advocate for Palestinian rights. The flotilla interception has been condemned by Turkey as 'piracy' and by Italy as 'unlawful,' and has triggered diplomatic pressure from Spain. The broader flotilla incident underlines the intensifying international dispute over Israel's enforcement of the Gaza naval blockade far from Gaza's coast.

media.caption: Spanish-Palestinian activist Saif Abukeshek returns to Barcelona defiant after six days in Israeli custody
